objects.definition: typedef locale_t mdb_locale_t;
objects.description: Alias for C locale_t used by mdbtools when iconv is unavailable to store/handle locale/encoding context.
Enumeration describing the table scan strategy chosen by the query planner.
Bitflags controlling file open behavior (e.g., writable). Used with mdb_open/mdb_open_buffer.
Enum specifying string format for GUID/UUID conversion.
Index metadata for a table, including key columns, order, flags, and first index page. Managed as part of a table’s indices.
Node in a selection-argument (SARG) expression tree used for filtering and index selection. Holds operator, column, literal value, and child pointers.
Describes a backend SQL type and which attributes (precision/scale/length) are required when emitting schema or data.
Pluggable backend configuration for exporting schema/data (SQL dialect specifics, type mappings, statements, formatting callbacks).
Optional statistics collector counting page reads when enabled.
Represents the underlying MDB/ACCDB file: FILE handle, version, free page map, code page, and stats. Typically internal to MdbHandle.
Version-specific constants and offsets for interpreting on-disk page and table layouts.

Primary context/handle for interacting with an MDB/ACCDB: buffers, format constants, backends, catalog, conversion settings, and I/O state. Create via mdb_open/mdb_open_buffer; clone with mdb_clone_handle; close with mdb_close.
Catalog item describing an object in the database (table, query, etc.), with name, type, and properties. Retrieved via catalog functions.
Name-keyed property set stored in a hash table for tables/columns/catalog entries.
Small tagged-union payload for SARG values: integer, double, or short string.
Column metadata and binding info for reading values, including properties, type, size, variable/fixed offsets, and SARG state.
Working state for an index page scan: positions, starts, cached values.

objects.definition: typedef int (*MdbSargTreeFunc)(MdbSargNode *, gpointer data);
objects.description: Callback type used when walking the SARG tree.
Holds traversal state across nested index pages during index scans/seek operations.

In-memory definition and state of a table: columns, indices, data/map pages, query strategy, and temp table support. Allocate/read via mdb_alloc_tabledef/mdb_read_table and free with mdb_free_tabledef.
Represents a column property entry name stub; details populated elsewhere. Limited usage info in header.
Describes a field value within a row buffer: pointers, sizes, offsets, null/fixed flags. Used when packing/inserting/updating rows.
Selection argument with operator and literal value used to build filter conditions and indexable predicates.
Duplicate of MdbIndexPage removed by deduplication. See MdbIndexPage above.
Duplicate of MdbIndexChain removed by deduplication. See MdbIndexChain above.

functions.name: mdb_get_version
functions.description: Returns a string with the MDB Tools library version. Typical use is for logging or displaying the library version.
requirements: Return value points to memory owned by the library; callers must not free it.

functions.name: mdb_read_pg
functions.description: Reads the specified database page number into the handle’s primary page buffer (pg_buf). Returns number of bytes read or a negative value on error.
requirements: mdb must be a valid, opened MdbHandle.
pg must refer to a valid page index in the database file.
Callers should check the return value for errors (<0) and short reads.

functions.name: mdb_read_alt_pg
functions.description: Reads the specified page into the handle’s alternate page buffer (alt_pg_buf). Returns number of bytes read or negative on error. Useful for comparing two pages simultaneously.
requirements: mdb must be a valid, opened MdbHandle.
pg must be a valid page index.
Check return value for errors (<0) and short reads.

functions.name: mdb_get_byte
functions.description: Reads a single byte at the given offset from an in-memory buffer containing MDB page or row data.
requirements: buf must point to a readable buffer with at least offset+1 bytes.
Offset must be within bounds of the buffer provided by the caller.

functions.name: mdb_get_int16
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit little-endian integer from the buffer at offset.
requirements: buf must point to a readable buffer containing at least offset+2 bytes.
Offset must be within bounds.

functions.name: mdb_get_int32
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit little-endian integer from the buffer at offset and returns it as long.
requirements: buf must point to a readable buffer containing at least offset+4 bytes.
Offset must be within bounds.

functions.name: mdb_get_int32_msb
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit big-endian integer (MSB first) from the buffer at offset and returns it as long.
requirements: buf must point to a readable buffer containing at least offset+4 bytes.
Offset must be within bounds.

functions.name: mdb_get_single
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit IEEE-754 float (little-endian) from the buffer at offset.
requirements: buf must point to at least offset+4 bytes.
Offset must be within bounds.

functions.name: mdb_get_double
functions.description: Reads a 64-bit IEEE-754 double (little-endian) from the buffer at offset.
requirements: buf must point to at least offset+8 bytes.
Offset must be within bounds.

functions.name: mdb_pg_get_byte
functions.description: Reads a byte from the current page buffer in mdb at the given offset.
requirements: mdb must be valid and a page must have been read into the buffer.
offset must be within page size (<= MDB_PGSIZE-1).

functions.name: mdb_pg_get_int16
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit little-endian integer from the handle’s current page buffer at offset.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a loaded page.
offset must allow reading 2 bytes within the page buffer.

functions.name: mdb_pg_get_int32
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit little-endian integer from the handle’s current page buffer at offset.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a loaded page.
offset must allow reading 4 bytes within the page buffer.

functions.name: mdb_pg_get_single
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit float from the handle’s current page buffer at offset.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a loaded page.
offset must allow reading 4 bytes within the page buffer.

functions.name: mdb_pg_get_double
functions.description: Reads a 64-bit double from the handle’s current page buffer at offset.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a loaded page.
offset must allow reading 8 bytes within the page buffer.

functions.name: mdb_open
functions.description: Opens an Access database file and returns a new MdbHandle for reading and optionally writing, based on flags.
requirements: filename must reference a readable MDB/ACCDB file path.
flags should be a valid combination of MdbFileFlags (e.g., MDB_NOFLAGS, MDB_WRITABLE).
Caller must eventually release the handle with mdb_close.
Check for NULL return indicating failure.

functions.name: mdb_open_buffer
functions.description: Creates an MdbHandle backed by an in-memory buffer containing an MDB/ACCDB image.
requirements: buffer must point to a readable memory region of size len.
len must be the complete database image size.
Caller must close with mdb_close.
Check for NULL return on failure.

functions.name: mdb_close
functions.description: Closes and frees an MdbHandle, releasing associated resources.
requirements: mdb must be a handle obtained from mdb_open/mdb_open_buffer or mdb_clone_handle.
Do not use mdb after this call.

functions.name: mdb_clone_handle
functions.description: Creates a clone of an existing handle for concurrent read operations sharing the same underlying file but with separate state buffers.
requirements: mdb must be a valid, open handle.
Caller must close the returned handle with mdb_close.
Check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: mdb_swap_pgbuf
functions.description: Swaps the primary and alternate page buffers in the handle, making the alternate buffer the current one.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
Assumes both buffers may contain previously read data; caller is responsible for ensuring buffer contents are meaningful before/after swap.

functions.name: mdb_free_catalog
functions.description: Frees catalog-related allocations attached to the handle (e.g., cached catalog entries).
requirements: mdb must be valid.
Should be called when catalog data is no longer needed or during cleanup.

functions.name: mdb_read_catalog
functions.description: Reads the database catalog entries of the specified object type and returns a pointer array of MdbCatalogEntry.
requirements: mdb must be valid and opened.
obj_type should be one of the MDB_* object type enums or MDB_ANY.
Caller is responsible for freeing the catalog via mdb_free_catalog or corresponding free routines.
Check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: mdb_get_catalogentry_by_name
functions.description: Finds a catalog entry by its object name and returns it if found.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have catalog data available (read via mdb_read_catalog or equivalent).
name must be a non-NULL string.
Check for NULL return if not found.

functions.name: mdb_dump_catalog
functions.description: Prints a human-readable dump of catalog entries of the specified type to stdout (or configured output). Intended for debugging or inspection.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
obj_type should be a valid MDB_* object type or MDB_ANY.

functions.name: mdb_get_objtype_string
functions.description: Returns a static string description for a catalog object type enum value.
requirements: obj_type must be a valid MDB_* object type; unknown values may map to a generic/unknown string.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: mdb_alloc_tabledef
functions.description: Allocates a new MdbTableDef associated with a catalog entry without fully reading its schema from disk.
requirements: entry must be a valid MdbCatalogEntry (typically from the catalog).
Caller must free with mdb_free_tabledef.
Check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: mdb_free_tabledef
functions.description: Frees an MdbTableDef and its associated allocations.
requirements: table must be a table definition previously allocated/returned by the library.
Do not use table after this call.

functions.name: mdb_read_table
functions.description: Reads a table definition and metadata for the given catalog entry and returns an initialized MdbTableDef.
requirements: entry must describe a table-like object.
Caller must free the result with mdb_free_tabledef.
Check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: mdb_read_table_by_name
functions.description: Looks up a table by name and type and returns its fully read MdbTableDef.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
table_name must be a valid, existing object name.
obj_type should be a valid MDB_* type (e.g., MDB_TABLE).
Caller must free the result with mdb_free_tabledef.
Check for NULL on failure or not found.

functions.name: mdb_append_column
functions.description: Appends a column definition to a GPtrArray of MdbColumn pointers.
requirements: columns must be a valid GPtrArray* intended to hold MdbColumn*.
in_col must be a valid MdbColumn* whose lifetime outlives the array or is managed appropriately.

functions.name: mdb_free_columns
functions.description: Frees a GPtrArray of MdbColumn objects and any owned column structures.
requirements: columns must be a GPtrArray* of MdbColumn pointers produced by this library.
Do not use the array or contained columns after freeing.

functions.name: mdb_read_columns
functions.description: Reads the column definitions for a table and returns them as a GPtrArray of MdbColumn.
requirements: table must be a valid MdbTableDef.
Caller should free the returned array with mdb_free_columns.
Check for NULL on failure.

functions.name: mdb_table_dump
functions.description: Dumps a human-readable representation of a table (or object) defined by the catalog entry to stdout. For debugging/inspection.
requirements: entry must reference a valid catalog entry for a table-like object.

functions.name: read_pg_if_8
functions.description: Reads an 8-bit value from the current page buffer at the position indicated by *cur_pos and advances the position.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a loaded page.
cur_pos must be non-NULL and point to a valid offset within the page; there must be at least 1 byte available.

functions.name: read_pg_if_16
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit little-endian value from the current page buffer at *cur_pos and advances the position accordingly.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a loaded page.
cur_pos must be non-NULL and allow reading 2 bytes within the page buffer.

functions.name: read_pg_if_32
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit little-endian value from the current page buffer at *cur_pos and advances the position.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a loaded page.
cur_pos must be non-NULL and allow reading 4 bytes within the page buffer.

functions.name: read_pg_if_n
functions.description: Reads len bytes from the current page buffer at *cur_pos into buf and advances the position. Returns buf.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a loaded page.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
cur_pos must be non-NULL and allow reading len bytes within the page buffer.

functions.name: mdb_is_user_table
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the catalog entry corresponds to a user table, zero otherwise.
requirements: entry must be a valid catalog entry.

functions.name: mdb_is_system_table
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the catalog entry is a system table, zero otherwise.
requirements: entry must be a valid catalog entry.

functions.name: mdb_table_get_prop
functions.description: Retrieves a table property value by key. Returns a string or NULL if not found.
requirements: table must be a valid table definition.
key must be a non-NULL string key.
Returned string is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: mdb_col_get_prop
functions.description: Retrieves a column property value by key. Returns a string or NULL if not found.
requirements: col must be a valid column descriptor.
key must be non-NULL.
Returned string is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: mdb_col_is_shortdate
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the column should be treated as a short date type according to backend/type metadata.
requirements: col must be valid.

functions.name: mdb_bind_column_by_name
functions.description: Binds a client buffer to receive data for a named column during row fetch. Typically used before calling mdb_fetch_row.
requirements: table must be a valid, opened table.
col_name must match an existing column name.
bind_ptr must point to a writable buffer of sufficient size (see mdb_set_bind_size or column size).
len_ptr may be NULL or must point to an int to receive the data length.
Returns 0/negative on failure; caller should check return code.

functions.name: mdb_data_dump
functions.description: Dumps table data rows in a human-readable format for debugging or inspection.
requirements: table must be a valid table definition with data accessible.

functions.name: mdb_date_to_tm
functions.description: Converts an MDB date/time stored as a double into a struct tm in UTC/localtime per library convention.
requirements: t must be a non-NULL pointer to a struct tm to receive the result.

functions.name: mdb_tm_to_date
functions.description: Converts a struct tm to the MDB double date/time representation.
requirements: t must be non-NULL and contain a valid broken-down time.
td must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the converted value.

functions.name: mdb_uuid_to_string
functions.description: Formats a UUID stored in buf at offset start into a newly allocated string using the default braces format. Caller typically frees the returned string.
requirements: buf must point to at least 16 bytes starting at offset start.
Returned string is heap-allocated by the library; caller should free it using the library’s allocator semantics (typically free()).

functions.name: mdb_uuid_to_string_fmt
functions.signature: char *mdb_uuid_to_string_fmt(const void *buf, int start, MdbUuidFormat format)
functions.description: Formats a UUID from buf at offset start into a newly allocated string using the specified format.
requirements: buf must contain at least 16 bytes at start.
format must be one of MdbUuidFormat values.
Caller should free the returned string when done.

functions.name: mdb_bind_column
functions.signature: int mdb_bind_column(MdbTableDef *table, int col_num, void *bind_ptr, int *len_ptr)
functions.description: Binds a client buffer to a column by index for subsequent fetches. Returns a status code.
requirements: table must be valid.
col_num must refer to an existing column index.
bind_ptr must be a writable buffer sized for the column’s output.
len_ptr may be NULL or must be a valid pointer to receive length.
Caller should check return code for success/failure.

functions.name: mdb_rewind_table
functions.description: Resets the table cursor to the beginning for iteration.
requirements: table must be valid.
Check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: mdb_fetch_row
functions.description: Advances to the next row and populates bound column buffers. Returns non-zero on success, 0 on EOF, or negative on error.
requirements: table must be valid and have columns bound as needed via mdb_bind_column/…
Caller must handle return values: 0 indicates no more rows; negative indicates error.

functions.name: mdb_is_fixed_col
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the column is fixed-length; zero if variable-length.
requirements: col must be valid.

functions.name: mdb_col_to_string
functions.signature: char *mdb_col_to_string(MdbHandle *mdb, void *buf, int start, int datatype, int size)
functions.description: Converts a raw column value from a buffer into a newly allocated string according to the given datatype and size.
requirements: mdb must be valid for formatting/locale info.
buf must contain the raw field bytes starting at offset start with at least size bytes available as required by datatype.
datatype must be one of the MDB_* type enums.
Caller should free the returned string.

functions.name: mdb_find_pg_row
functions.signature: int mdb_find_pg_row(MdbHandle *mdb, int pg_row, void **buf, int *off, size_t *len)
functions.description: Locates a row within the current page (by page-local row index) and returns its buffer pointer, offset, and length.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a current page loaded.
buf must be non-NULL and will receive a pointer to the page buffer.
off and len must be non-NULL to receive row start offset and length.
pg_row must refer to a valid row number on the current page.
Caller must check return code for success (non-zero) or failure.

functions.name: mdb_find_row
functions.signature: int mdb_find_row(MdbHandle *mdb, int row, int *start, size_t *len)
functions.description: Finds the position and length of a logical row in the current context and returns them via start and len.
requirements: mdb must be valid and positioned appropriately.
start and len must be non-NULL.
row must be a valid row index in the relevant page/table context.
Caller must check the return code.

functions.name: mdb_find_end_of_row
functions.description: Returns the byte offset of the end of the specified row in the current page or a status code if not found.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a current page.
row must be valid within the current page context.
Caller must check return value for errors.

functions.name: mdb_col_fixed_size
functions.description: Returns the fixed byte size for a fixed-length column type, or 0/negative for variable or unknown.
requirements: col must be valid.

functions.name: mdb_col_disp_size
functions.description: Returns a recommended display width/size for the column type.
requirements: col must be valid.

functions.name: mdb_ole_read_next
functions.description: Reads the next chunk of an OLE (blob/memo) field referenced by ole_ptr into an internal buffer or advances internal OLE reading state. Returns number of bytes read.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
col must be an OLE/MEMO-capable column context initialized via a prior read.
ole_ptr must be a pointer previously obtained for OLE reading (library-specific).
Caller must check the returned size; 0 may indicate end-of-stream.

functions.name: mdb_ole_read
functions.signature: size_t mdb_ole_read(MdbHandle *mdb, MdbColumn *col, void *ole_ptr, size_t chunk_size)
functions.description: Reads up to chunk_size bytes from an OLE (blob/memo) field referred by ole_ptr.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
col must be appropriate for OLE/MEMO data.
ole_ptr must be a valid OLE reference.
chunk_size specifies the maximum bytes to read and should be > 0.

functions.name: mdb_ole_read_full
functions.description: Reads the entire OLE/MEMO field for the column and returns a newly allocated buffer containing the data and its size via size.
requirements: mdb and col must be valid and point at a current row/field containing OLE data.
size must be non-NULL to receive data size.
Caller must free the returned buffer when done.
Check for NULL return on failure.

functions.name: mdb_set_bind_size
functions.description: Sets the default maximum buffer size used for bound column values.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
bind_size should be a reasonable size for expected column data; very small sizes may truncate; very large may impact memory.

functions.name: mdb_set_date_fmt
functions.description: Sets the long date/time output format string for date conversions to string.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
Format string must be a valid strftime-like format expected by the library.

functions.name: mdb_set_shortdate_fmt
functions.description: Sets the short date output format string used when formatting short dates.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
Format string must be valid per library expectations.

functions.name: mdb_set_repid_fmt
functions.description: Sets the formatting style for REPID/UUID output when converting to strings.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
format must be a valid MdbUuidFormat value.

functions.name: mdb_set_boolean_fmt_words
functions.description: Configures boolean output formatting to use words (e.g., true/false) when converting to strings.
requirements: mdb must be valid.

functions.name: mdb_set_boolean_fmt_numbers
functions.description: Configures boolean output formatting to use numeric values (e.g., 0/1) when converting to strings.
requirements: mdb must be valid.

functions.name: mdb_read_row
functions.description: Reads and parses the specified row number from the table into internal/bound buffers. Returns status.
requirements: table must be valid.
row must be a valid row index within the table.
Caller should check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: mdb_read_next_dpg
functions.description: Advances to and reads the next data page for the table. Returns status.
requirements: table must be valid and associated with an open handle.
Caller should check the return value for success/failure or EOF state.

functions.name: mdb_money_to_string
functions.description: Converts a MONEY value at offset start in the current page/buffer into a newly allocated string using handle locale/format.
requirements: mdb must be valid and buffer positioned appropriately for reading the value at start.
Caller should free the returned string.

functions.name: mdb_numeric_to_string
functions.signature: char *mdb_numeric_to_string(MdbHandle *mdb, int start, int scale, int prec)
functions.description: Converts a NUMERIC/DECIMAL value at offset start into a newly allocated string using provided scale and precision.
requirements: mdb must be valid and buffer contain the numeric value at start.
scale and prec must match the value’s definition.
Caller should free the returned string.

functions.name: mdb_buffer_dump
functions.signature: void mdb_buffer_dump(const void *buf, off_t start, size_t len)
functions.description: Hex-dumps len bytes from buf starting at offset start to stdout for debugging.
requirements: buf must point to at least start+len bytes readable.

functions.name: mdb_init_backends
functions.description: Initializes built-in/export backends (DDL/export type mappings) for the handle.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
Call before using backend-dependent features (schema export/type mapping).

functions.name: mdb_remove_backends
functions.description: Unregisters and frees backend definitions attached to the handle.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
Should be called during cleanup when backends are no longer needed.

functions.name: mdb_get_colbacktype
functions.description: Returns the backend type mapping for a given column according to the current backend.
requirements: col must be valid and associated with a table whose handle has initialized backends.
Return pointer is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: mdb_get_colbacktype_string
functions.description: Returns a string name of the backend-mapped type for the column.
requirements: col must be valid and backends must be initialized.
Returned string is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: mdb_colbacktype_takes_length
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the backend type for the column requires a length specification (e.g., VARCHAR(n)).
requirements: col must be valid and backends initialized.

functions.name: mdb_register_backend
functions.description: Registers a backend definition (DDL/type mapping and formatting parameters) under a name for use with schema export and type mapping.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
backend_name must be a non-NULL identifier string.
Function pointers and strings provided must remain valid for the lifetime of the backend registration unless copied internally.
capabilities should be a combination of MDB_SHEXP_* flags.

functions.name: mdb_set_default_backend
functions.description: Sets the default backend by name for the handle, affecting type mapping and schema export. Returns status.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have the backend registered via mdb_register_backend/mdb_init_backends.
backend_name must match a registered backend.
Caller should check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: mdb_print_schema
functions.signature: int  mdb_print_schema(MdbHandle *mdb, FILE *outfile, char *tabname, char *dbnamespace, guint32 export_options)
functions.description: Prints CREATE TABLE and related schema DDL for a table (or entire DB) to outfile using the selected backend and export options. Returns status.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have backends initialized.
outfile must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
tabname may be NULL to print all tables or a specific table name.
dbnamespace may be NULL or a target schema/namespace string.
export_options must use MDB_SHEXP_* flags.
Check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: mdb_print_col
functions.signature: void mdb_print_col(FILE *outfile, gchar *col_val, int quote_text, int col_type, int bin_len, char *quote_char, char *escape_char, int flags)
functions.description: Prints a single column value to outfile with appropriate quoting/escaping based on type and flags, for data export (e.g., CSV/SQL).
requirements: outfile must be a valid writable FILE*.
col_val must be a valid string for text types or formatted binary text for others as expected.
quote_text indicates whether to quote text values (non-zero).
col_type must be a valid MDB_* type.
quote_char and escape_char may be NULL to use defaults or must be single-character strings if provided.
flags may include MDB_EXPORT_ESCAPE_CONTROL_CHARS and binary export mode selection.

functions.name: mdb_normalise_and_replace
functions.description: Normalises a string according to backend rules and possibly replaces the original pointer, returning the new string.
requirements: mdb must be valid and have a backend selected.
str must be a non-NULL pointer to a gchar*; function may modify or replace *str.
Returned string is allocated; caller must free if ownership is transferred (library-specific).

functions.name: mdb_test_sargs
functions.description: Evaluates all search arguments (SARGs) attached to the table against the provided fields to determine if a row matches. Returns non-zero if match.
requirements: table must be valid and may have sargs set.
fields must describe the current row’s fields; length must be num_fields.
Caller must check return value for match/non-match.

functions.name: mdb_test_sarg
functions.description: Evaluates a single SARG node against a field value for a given column. Returns non-zero if the predicate matches.
requirements: mdb must be valid.
col must be the target column descriptor.
node must be a valid SARG tree node.
field must be a valid field representation for the row.

functions.name: mdb_sql_walk_tree
functions.signature: void mdb_sql_walk_tree(MdbSargNode *node, MdbSargTreeFunc func, gpointer data)
functions.description: Traverses a SARG tree and calls func for each node, passing data as user context.
requirements: node may be NULL (no-op) or a valid tree root.
func must be a valid callback function pointer; it should tolerate being called with various node types.
data is user-provided context and may be NULL.

functions.name: mdb_find_indexable_sargs
functions.description: Analyzes a SARG tree to locate predicates that can be satisfied using an index. Returns a count/status.
requirements: node must be a valid SARG tree or NULL.
data is context-dependent and may be NULL.

functions.name: mdb_add_sarg_by_name
functions.description: Adds a search argument predicate for a named column to the table’s SARG list. Returns status.
requirements: table must be valid.
colname must be a valid column name.
in_sarg must point to a valid MdbSarg structure describing the predicate.
Caller should check return value for success/failure.

functions.name: mdb_test_string
functions.description: Tests a string value s against the predicate represented by node (e.g., LIKE/ILIKE/EQUAL). Returns non-zero on match.
requirements: node must be a valid SARG node representing a string comparison.
s must be a valid NUL-terminated string (may be NULL depending on operator semantics).

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces arbitrary binary buffers that are valid for the target
# fuzz stubs which read primitive values (byte/int16/int32/float/double), UUIDs,
# and generic slices. We try to create buffers of varying sizes and contents that
# remain valid for the stubs' minimum length requirements and exercise different
# code paths (endianness, numeric ranges, NaNs/Infs, UUID patterns, text-like regions,
# repeating bytes, zero-filled, random data, etc.).

# We avoid any post-generation mutation; outputs are valid buffers up to 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Predefined interesting 16-byte UUID-like values
UUID_PATTERNS: List[bytes] = [
    # All zeros
    b"\x00" * 16,
    # All 0xFF
    b"\xFF" * 16,
    # Nil UUID
    bytes.fromhex("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000".replace("-", "")),
    # Version 4, random variant
    bytes.fromhex("123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426655440000".replace("-", "")),
    # Version 1-ish
    bytes.fromhex("00112233-4455-6677-8899-aabbccddeeff".replace("-", "")),
]

# Predefined interesting 4-byte (float/int32) and 8-byte (double) values
INTERESTING_INT32 = [
    0, 1, -1 & 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFFF,
    0x11223344, 0xAABBCCDD,
]

INTERESTING_FLOAT32 = [
    0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 3.1415927, float('inf'), float('-inf'),
]
# A quiet NaN bit pattern (platform independent assembly)
QUIET_NAN_F32 = struct.pack('<I', 0x7FC00000)

INTERESTING_FLOAT64 = [
    0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 3.141592653589793, float('inf'), float('-inf'),
]
QUIET_NAN_F64 = struct.pack('<Q', 0x7FF8000000000000)

TEXT_SNIPPETS = [
    b"Hello, world!", b"Test", b"", b"%LIKE_pattern%", b"_single_char_",
    b"GUID:{01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef}",
    b"{DEADBEEF-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}",
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _emit_uuid_region(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a UUID pattern and optionally tweak a few bytes
    base = bytearray(rng.choice(UUID_PATTERNS))
    # With some probability, introduce slight randomness to still valid size
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        idx = rng.randrange(16)
        base[idx] = rng.randrange(256)
    return bytes(base)


def _emit_numeric_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # Add several int32 (LE), int32 (BE), float32, float64 sequences
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        v = rng.choice(INTERESTING_INT32)
        out += struct.pack('<I', v)
        out += struct.pack('>I', v)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
        v = rng.choice(INTERESTING_FLOAT32)
        out += struct.pack('<f', v)
        out += QUIET_NAN_F32
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
        v = rng.choice(INTERESTING_FLOAT64)
        out += struct.pack('<d', v)
        out += QUIET_NAN_F64
    return bytes(out)


def _emit_text_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        p = rng.choice(TEXT_SNIPPETS)
        # Sometimes pad or include NULs
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            p += b"\x00" * rng.randint(1, 4)
        parts.append(p)
    # Optionally add ASCII range random text
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ln = rng.randint(4, 32)
        ascii_bytes = bytes(rng.randrange(32, 127) for _ in range(ln))
        parts.append(ascii_bytes)
    return b"".join(parts)


def _emit_pattern_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Repeating byte patterns, incremental counters, zero/FF runs
    choice = rng.randrange(5)
    if choice == 0:
        bval = rng.randrange(256)
        return bytes([bval]) * rng.randint(4, 64)
    elif choice == 1:
        # 0..255 cycling sequence slice
        ln = rng.randint(16, 128)
        return bytes((i % 256 for i in range(rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256) + ln)))
    elif choice == 2:
        return b"\x00" * rng.randint(8, 128)
    elif choice == 3:
        return b"\xFF" * rng.randint(8, 128)
    else:
        # Random chunk
        return _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(8, 128))


def _compose_buffer(rng: random.Random, target_min: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose from multiple regions to satisfy various stubs: need at least up to 16 bytes
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Ensure we have at least one UUID region for uuid_to_string* stubs
    chunks.append(_emit_uuid_region(rng))

    # Add numeric data for mdb_get_* reads
    chunks.append(_emit_numeric_block(rng))

    # Add some text/patterns for buffer_dump and potential col_to_string
    chunks.append(_emit_text_block(rng))
    chunks.append(_emit_pattern_block(rng))

    # Optionally add more random data to vary size
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        chunks.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 256)))

    buf = b"".join(chunks)

    # Ensure minimum size
    if len(buf) < target_min:
        buf += _rand_bytes(rng, target_min - len(buf))

    # Cap to MAX_SIZE
    if len(buf) > MAX_SIZE:
        buf = buf[:MAX_SIZE]

    return buf


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a target minimum length required by random fuzzer stub selection
    # The stubs require at least 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16 bytes depending on function.

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces a minimal, self-consistent Microsoft Jet (MDB) database
# image (Jet 3.x/4.x style) sufficient for mdb_open/mdb_open_buffer to consider it
# a plausible database and proceed. We craft a header and a couple of pages with
# reasonable values. The goal is valid-looking, not exhaustive correctness.
#
# Strategy:
# - Page size 4096 bytes (common for Jet4). Total size is multiple of page size.
# - Page 0: Database header with signature, format/version, page size, code page.
# - Page 1: Minimal catalog-like page stub; contents are benign padding.
# - Optionally sprinkle some recognizable text and valid little-endian fields.
#
# We avoid external I/O and keep total size <= 4096*2.

PAGE_SIZE = 4096
TOTAL_PAGES_MIN = 2

# Jet4 MDB header signature (first 16 bytes):
# 0x00-0x03: 0x00 0x01 0x00 0x00 (magic)
# 0x04-0x07: 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00 (version/page bits)
# 0x08-0x0B: 0x00 0x00 0x01 0x00 (obuf?) varies, but many tools check fixed bytes
# 0x0C-0x0F: 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00
# However, MDB Tools typically recognizes Jet via text signature at offset 0x14:
# "Standard Jet DB" and a format byte at 0x00.
# For robustness we include the string and set page size field.

JET_HEADER_STRING = b"Standard Jet DB"


def _le16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', x & 0xFFFF)


def _le32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _be32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _init_page(size: int) -> bytearray:
    return bytearray(b"\x00" * size)


def _build_header(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed + 1)
    p = _init_page(PAGE_SIZE)

    # Many MDB parsers expect specific fields:
    # 0x00: dbType (1 for Jet3, 0 for Jet4). We'll use 0 for Jet4.
    p[0x00] = 0

    # 0x01: unknown flag, keep 0
    p[0x01] = 0

    # 0x02-0x03: Jet version (0x0001 or 0x0000). Use 0x0000 for Jet4
    p[0x02:0x04] = _le16(0)

    # 0x04-0x13: reserved/zero
    # 0x14-0x23: "Standard Jet DB"
    p[0x14:0x14 + len(JET_HEADER_STRING)] = JET_HEADER_STRING

    # 0x24: version byte; 0 for Jet4, 1 for Jet3
    p[0x24] = 0

    # 0x28-0x29: page size (little-endian). Put 4096
    p[0x28:0x2A] = _le16(PAGE_SIZE)

    # 0x2A-0x2B: code page (e.g., 1252). Choose 1252 or 1200 for Unicode.
    code_page = rnd.choice([1200, 1252, 65001])  # 1200=UTF-16LE, 1252=Windows Latin1, 65001=UTF-8 (non-standard)
    p[0x2A:0x2C] = _le16(code_page if code_page != 65001 else 1252)

    # 0x2C-0x2F: sort order/lang id. Use 0x0409 (en-US)
    p[0x2C:0x30] = _le32(0x0409)

    # 0x30-0x33: db key (random)
    p[0x30:0x34] = _le32(rnd.getrandbits(32))

    # 0x34-0x41: database password obfuscation storage (14 bytes). Zero/seeded
    pw = bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(14))
    p[0x34:0x34 + 14] = pw

    # Fill some plausible fields to satisfy offset lookups used later by helpers
    # First data page number (make it 1)
    p[0x78:0x7C] = _le32(1)

    # Jet version full (store again later)
    p[0x60:0x64] = _le32(0x00000000)

    # Put some strings for charset/locale queries to not crash string scans
    banner = b"MDBToolsCompat\0"
    p[0x100:0x100 + len(banner)] = banner

    # Ensure the page checksum/simple sum may look consistent; many MDBs do not
    # require, so leave zeros.
    return bytes(p)


def _build_simple_data_page(seed: int, pgno: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed + 100 + pgno)
    p = _init_page(PAGE_SIZE)

    # Page header: first two bytes often indicate number of rows; put a small value.
    num_rows = rnd.randint(0, 3)
    p[0x00:0x02] = _le16(num_rows)

    # Next 2 bytes: free space or row start pointer; we craft a simple layout.
    # We'll create a single trivial row directory at end of page.
    row_offsets: List[int] = []
    cursor = 0x40  # start of row data region

    for i in range(num_rows):
        # Simple row: length-prefixed blob with ASCII text and an int
        text = f"Row{i}_Seed{seed}".encode('ascii')
        val = rnd.randint(-1000, 1000)
        row = bytearray()
        row += _le16(len(text))
        row += text
        row += _le32(val & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        # Write row
        end = cursor + len(row)
        if end >= PAGE_SIZE - 2 * (num_rows + 1):
            break
        p[cursor:end] = row
        row_offsets.append(cursor)
        cursor = end

    # Directory: write row start offsets at end of page, little-endian 16-bit
    dir_start = PAGE_SIZE - 2 * max(1, len(row_offsets))
    offs = row_offsets if row_offsets else [0]
    for i, ro in enumerate(offs):
        p[dir_start + 2 * i:dir_start + 2 * i + 2] = _le16(ro)

    # Update number of rows and free space pointer if we populated rows
    p[0x00:0x02] = _le16(len(row_offsets))
    p[0x02:0x04] = _le16(cursor)  # simple free space pointer approximation

    # Store a pseudo page type marker at a common offset to resemble data page
    p[0x08] = 0x01  # arbitrary non-zero

    return bytes(p)


def _choose_total_pages(rnd: random.Random) -> int:
    return rnd.choice([2, 3, 4])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    total_pages = max(TOTAL_PAGES_MIN, _choose_total_pages(rnd))

    pages: List[bytes] = []
    pages.append(_build_header(seed))

    # First data/catalog-like page
    pages.append(_build_simple_data_page(seed, 1))

    # Optional extra pages
    for i in range(2, total_pages):
        pages.append(_build_simple_data_page(seed, i))

    img = b"".join(pages)
    # Ensure size is multiple of PAGE_SIZE and <= 4096*4 (we cap total_pages)
    return img[: PAGE_SIZE * total_pages]

import random
import struct
import time

# This generator crafts a minimal-but-valid-ish Jet (MDB) database image.
# Goal: be accepted by mdb_open_buffer and allow page reads. We construct
# a simple JET3/4-style header and a small number of pages with sane fields.
# It does not need to be a fully consistent DB, just structurally plausible.

# Constants inspired by Jet (MDB) layout basics
PG_SIZE = 4096  # Common Jet3/4 page size

# Database format signature and markers
MAGIC = b"Standard Jet DB"
MAGIC2 = b"Jet"

# Helpers

def le16(v):
    return struct.pack('<H', v & 0xFFFF)

def le32(v):
    return struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def be32(v):
    return struct.pack('>I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def pad_to(data: bytearray, size: int, fill: int = 0):
    if len(data) < size:
        data += bytes([fill]) * (size - len(data))
    return data

# Build a plausible header page (page 0)
# Not a full, exact replica; sufficient fields placed at conventional offsets used by many parsers.
# Layout references (approximate for fuzz seeding):
#   0x00: "Standard Jet DB" (16 bytes)
#   0x10: Version (e.g., 0x0001 0x0000) or similar
#   0x14: DB Key (random)
#   0x18: Creation/format markers
#   0x20..: free map references, first data page, code page, etc.

def build_header_page(rng: random.Random, total_pages: int, jet_version: int, codepage: int, lang_id: int, db_key: int) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray(PG_SIZE)
    # Signature
    b[0:len(MAGIC)] = MAGIC
    # Basic versioning/markers
    # Many tools check for these strings and a reasonable page size and version.
    # Place a secondary marker to increase plausibility
    b[0x40:0x40+len(MAGIC2)] = MAGIC2

    # Jet version at some common offsets used by parsers (not authoritative but plausible)
    # Store at 0x14 (db_key) and 0x18 (jet version)
    # db_key (random 32-bit)
    b[0x14:0x18] = le32(db_key)

    # Jet version (pick between common 0x00000003 or 0x00000004)
    b[0x18:0x1C] = le32(jet_version)

    # Page size at 0x1C
    b[0x1C:0x20] = le32(PG_SIZE)

    # Code page / language id at conventional-ish locations (not exact, but consistent)
    b[0x20:0x22] = le16(codepage)
    b[0x22:0x24] = le16(lang_id)

    # Total pages
    b[0x24:0x28] = le32(total_pages)

    # First catalog page pointer (set to page 1)
    b[0x28:0x2C] = le32(1 if total_pages > 1 else 0)

    # Free map base page (point somewhere plausible, say page 2)
    freemap_base = 2 if total_pages > 3 else 0
    b[0x2C:0x30] = le32(freemap_base)

    # Set a few more integers to non-zero to look realistic
    b[0x30:0x34] = le32(0x00010000)  # format flags/version minor
    b[0x34:0x38] = le32(int(time.time()) & 0xFFFFFFFF)  # timestamp-ish

    # Simple checksum at end (not real Jet checksum, just non-zero data)
    b[-4:] = le32(sum(b[:PG_SIZE-4]) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(b)

# Build a simple catalog-like page (page 1). We place a small header and a single row-ish structure.
# The library often scans catalog; even if it later fails, the handle will be created.

def build_catalog_page(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray(PG_SIZE)
    # Page type marker at start (arbitrary non-zero type)
    b[0:2] = le16(0x0001)
    # Row count
    b[2:4] = le16(1)
    # Row offset table at end of page (typical Jet has row offsets at the end)
    # Place one small row starting near 0x80
    row_start = 0x80
    row_len = 32
    # Create a trivial row with a name-like bytes and type
    row = bytearray(row_len)
    name = b"Table1\x00"
    row[0:len(name)] = name
    # object type
    row[16:20] = le32(1)  # user table
    # first data page pointer
    row[20:24] = le32(3)
    b[row_start:row_start+row_len] = row

    # Write row offset at end-of-page
    b[-2:] = le16(row_start)

    # Simple header fields near start to be plausible
    b[4:8] = le32(row_len)
    b[8:12] = le32(0)  # flags

    # checksum-ish
    b[-4:] = le32((sum(b[:-4]) + 12345) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(b)

# Build a free map page (bitmap). We'll set a few bits to indicate used pages.

def build_freemap_page(total_pages: int) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray(PG_SIZE)
    # Mark pages 0..(n) as used
    used_pages = min(total_pages, 16)
    for pg in range(used_pages):
        byte_idx = pg // 8
        bit = pg % 8
        if byte_idx < PG_SIZE:
            b[byte_idx] |= (1 << bit)
    # checksum-ish
    b[-4:] = le32(sum(b[:-4]) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(b)

# Build a simple data page with a single small row

def build_data_page(rng: random.Random, text: bytes) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray(PG_SIZE)
    # Page type marker
    b[0:2] = le16(0x0002)
    # Place a single row
    start = 0x60
    max_text = min(len(text), 80)
    row = text[:max_text]
    b[start:start+len(row)] = row
    # Row count
    b[2:4] = le16(1)
    # Row length stored in header
    b[4:8] = le32(len(row))
    # Row offset at end
    b[-2:] = le16(start)
    # checksum-ish
    b[-4:] = le32((sum(b[:-4]) ^ 0xA5A5A5A5) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(b)


def build_image(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Randomize number of pages within reasonable bounds but >= 4
    total_pages = rng.randint(4, 16)

    # Choose a plausible Jet version
    jet_version = rng.choice([3, 4])

    # Random but plausible code page and language id
    codepage = rng.choice([1252, 65001, 28591, 936]) & 0xFFFF
    lang_id = rng.choice([0x0409, 0x0000, 0x0407, 0x0411]) & 0xFFFF

    db_key = rng.getrandbits(32)

    pages = []
    pages.append(build_header_page(rng, total_pages, jet_version, codepage, lang_id, db_key))
    pages.append(build_catalog_page(rng))
    pages.append(build_freemap_page(total_pages))

    # Fill remaining pages with data pages containing seeded text
    base_texts = [
        b"hello, world",
        b"Sample row data for mdbtools fuzz seed",
        b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
        b"GUID: 00112233445566778899AABBCCDDEEFF",
    ]
    for i in range(3, total_pages):
        txt = rng.choice(base_texts)
        # Add some random printable padding
        extra = bytes(rng.choices(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 ", k=rng.randint(0, 32)))
        pages.append(build_data_page(rng, txt + extra))

    img = b"".join(pages)
    # Ensure size >= 512 and <= 4096*16 by construction. Return as bytes.
    return img


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Occasionally vary page size marker by building multiple-of-4096 images (still PG_SIZE used internally)
    img = build_image(rng)

    # Truncate to <= 4096 bytes if randomly desired? The fuzzer requires >=512, but library expects full image.
    # We keep full image but ensure under 4096 bytes limit from instruction. If larger, trim at 4096 keeping full pages.
    if len(img) > 4096:
        # Keep first 4096 bytes (one page). Still carries header + some structure; acceptable for handle open tests.
        img = img[:4096]
        # Recompute checksum at end of page since we cut
        b = bytearray(img)
        b[-4:] = le32(sum(b[:-4]) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        img = bytes(b)

    # Ensure minimum length 512
    if len(img) < 512:
        img += bytes(512 - len(img))

    return img

import random

# This generator targets inputs where FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME are consumed.
# The target library uses many NUL-terminated strings for names, identifiers, backend names,
# table/column names, LIKE patterns, and general text. We generate a composite buffer that
# encodes a sequence of interesting strings and a filename path. The harness will read these
# sequentially via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and integers/doubles as needed.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a corpus of plausible identifiers and names that increase the chance of finding
#   existing objects in a typical Access DB (e.g., common system tables, columns, keywords).
# - Include LIKE patterns with %, _, bracket classes, and escaping to exercise like/ilike.
# - Provide short backend names and safe filenames.
# - Mix in varying lengths (empty, 1-char, typical, max-limited) while keeping them valid.
# - ASCII/UTF-8 content including spaces, punctuation and some unicode to exercise conversions.
# - Separate strings with NUL bytes so that the fuzz harness can treat each FUZZ_PARAM_STR as a
#   C-string slice from the buffer. FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME also expects a NUL-terminated path.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Buffer layout (all NUL-terminated C strings in sequence):
#   [S0]\0 [S1]\0 ... [Sk]\0
# The fuzzer will consume them in order for FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME calls.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

COMMON_TABLE_NAMES = [
    "MSysObjects", "MSysACEs", "MSysQueries", "MSysRelationships", "MSysAccessStorage",
    "MSysAccessXML", "MSysModules", "MSysModules2", "MSysRelationships2", "MSysNavPaneGroupCategories",
    "MSysNameMap",
    "Tables", "Columns", "Indices", "Relationships", "Queries",
]

COMMON_COLUMN_NAMES = [
    "ID", "Name", "Description", "Created", "Modified", "Owner", "Type", "Flags",
    "ParentID", "ObjectID", "Date", "Time", "Timestamp", "Value", "Data", "Blob",
]

# Some reasonable backend names/dialects seen in exporters
BACKEND_NAMES = [
    "access", "mysql", "postgres", "sqlite", "mssql", "oracle", "csv", "sybase", "firebird",
]

LIKE_PATTERNS = [
    "%", "_", "%a%", "a_c", "[A-Z]%", "[a-z]_%", "%[0-9]%", "a%_b", "%\\_%", "a[]b",
    "[^a]%", "a%b%c", "%abc", "abc%", "%a_c%", "[!A]b%",
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "naïve", "café", "über", "δοκιμή", "тест", "テスト", "測試", "اختبار", "emoji🙂", "雪", "España",
]

SAFE_FILENAME_PARTS = [
    "out", "tmp", "schema", "data", "export", "table", "column", "idx", "text", "log",
]

EXTS = [".txt", ".csv", ".sql", ".out", ".log"]

IDENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)  # start with letter
    if n > 1:
        s += "".join(rng.choice(IDENT_CHARS) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s


def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]


def make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a POSIX-like path under /tmp to ensure open("wb") success in most harnesses
    parts = ["/tmp"]
    # one or two subdirs to vary path depth
    depth = 1 if rng.random() < 0.7 else 2
    for _ in range(depth):
        part = rand_choice(rng, SAFE_FILENAME_PARTS)
        # avoid excessively long names
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            part += "_" + rand_ident(rng, 1, 6)
        parts.append(part)
    base = rand_choice(rng, SAFE_FILENAME_PARTS)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        base += "_" + rand_ident(rng, 1, 8)
    ext = rand_choice(rng, EXTS)
    parts[-1] = base + ext
    path = "/".join(parts)
    return path


def build_string_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool: List[str] = []

    # 1) Candidate names likely to succeed for catalog/table lookups
    pool += COMMON_TABLE_NAMES
    pool += COMMON_COLUMN_NAMES

    # 2) Backend names including short/1-char variants
    pool += BACKEND_NAMES
    pool += ["b", "pg", "my", "zz", "zztmp"]

    # 3) Like/ILike patterns
    pool += LIKE_PATTERNS

    # 4) Random identifiers and longer names
    for _ in range(10):
        pool.append(rand_ident(rng, 1, 10))
    for _ in range(5):
        pool.append(rand_ident(rng, 8, 20))

    # 5) Various lengths including empty and max-ish
    pool.append("")  # sometimes allowed (interpreted as NULL in stubs)
    pool.append("x")
    pool.append("y" * 32)
    pool.append("z" * 64)

    # 6) Unicode samples for conversion paths
    pool += UNICODE_SAMPLES

    # 7) Formatting strings for date outputs (strftime-like) to be used by setters
    pool += ["%Y-%m-%d", "%F %T", "%m/%d/%Y", "%d.%m.%Y", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"]

    # 8) Some probable table and namespace names used by print_schema
    pool += ["public", "dbo", "main", "default", "sales", "inventory"]

    # Shuffle and trim duplicates while preserving order
    seen = set()
    deduped: List[str] = []
    for s in pool:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            deduped.append(s)
    rng.shuffle(deduped)

    # Add additional random LIKE patterns and text blobs
    for _ in range(8):
        # mixture of alpha, space, punctuation to test quoting/escaping
        length = rng.randint(1, 40)
        alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-%[]!#@$^,."
        txt = "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
        # occasionally wrap with % for like patterns
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            txt = ("%" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "") + txt + ("%" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "")
        deduped.append(txt)

    # Ensure presence of a few specific values helpful for fallbacks
    for s in ["zztmp", "TEXT", "INT"]:
        if s not in deduped:
            deduped.append(s)

    return deduped


def encode_cstrings(strings: List[str], limit: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        # respect individual string cap to avoid giant entries
        if len(b) > 512:
            b = b[:512]
        if len(out) + len(b) + 1 > limit:
            break
        out += b
        out.append(0)
    # Ensure at least one filename path at the end for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
    # Append as another NUL-terminated string
    fn = make_filename(rng).encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(out) + len(fn) + 1 <= limit:
        out += fn
        out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strings = build_string_pool(rng)

    # Interleave with extra entries to align with multiple stubs consuming strings
    # Add a couple of table names and column names again to increase hit rate
    extras = []
    for _ in range(3):
        extras.append(rand_choice(rng, COMMON_TABLE_NAMES))
        extras.append(rand_choice(rng, COMMON_COLUMN_NAMES))
        extras.append(rand_choice(rng, BACKEND_NAMES))
        extras.append(rand_choice(rng, LIKE_PATTERNS))
    rng.shuffle(extras)
    strings = extras + strings

    buf = encode_cstrings(strings, MAX_TOTAL, rng)
    return buf

    return choices[-1]

def _build_pattern(rng, max_len):
    # With some probability, pick a themed pattern then decorate
    if rng.random() < 0.40:
        base = rng.choice(THEMES)
        pat = base
        # Sprinkle some literals or extra directives at start/end
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pat = rng.choice(LITERALS) + pat
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pat = pat + rng.choice(LITERALS)
    else:
        # Construct by alternating directives and literals
        parts = []
        # Start with a directive to ensure meaningful content
        parts.append(rng.choice(DIRECTIVES))
        # Add a random number of segments
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8)):
            if rng.random() < 0.75:
                parts.append(rng.choice(LITERALS))
            parts.append(rng.choice(DIRECTIVES))
        pat = "".join(parts)

    # Occasionally wrap with edge literals
    if rng.random() < 0.20:
        wrap = rng.choice(EDGE_LITERALS)
        pat = wrap + pat + wrap

    # Ensure not empty and trim to max_len
    if not pat:
        pat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
    if len(pat) > max_len:
        pat = pat[:max_len]
    # Avoid ending with stray single percent which would be invalid for strftime
    if pat.endswith('%'):
        pat = pat[:-1] + '%%'
    # Also avoid any isolated '%' occurrences (very rare with our construction)
    # Replace any single '%' not followed by a valid directive char with '%%'
    out = []
    i = 0
    valid_next = set(ch[1] for ch in DIRECTIVES if len(ch) == 2) | set(['%'])
    while i < len(pat):
        ch = pat[i]
        if ch == '%':
            if i + 1 >= len(pat):
                out.append('%%')
                i += 1
                continue
            nxt = pat[i+1]
            if nxt in valid_next:
                out.append('%' + nxt)
                i += 2
            else:
                out.append('%%')
                i += 1
        else:
            out.append(ch)
            i += 1
    pat = "".join(out)
    # Final length cap
    if len(pat) > max_len:
        pat = pat[:max_len]
    # Guarantee non-empty
    if not pat:
        pat = "%c"
    return pat

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Target length: up to 63 bytes, but vary length to explore parser
    max_len = rng.randint(8, 63)

    # Build between 1 and 3 patterns separated by newline, as fuzzer may request multiple values
    # but our buffer will be consumed as a single FUZZ_PARAM_STR. To serve both date_fmt and
    # shortdate_fmt fuzzers, we produce a single valid format string (no newlines).
    pattern = _build_pattern(rng, max_len)

    # Return as bytes (UTF-8). Avoid exceeding 4096 bytes.
    data = pattern.encode('utf-8')
    if not data:
        data = b"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
